# Agenda

- Why feature engineering matters
- Review of handy transformation verbs (`mutate`, `across`, `case_when`)
- Building new predictors from Laser League data
- Documenting assumptions + storing engineered tables for modeling

---

# Why Feature Engineering?

- Raw data rarely captures the true signal
- Transformations expose relationships models can learn
- Helps normalize scale, reduce skew, encode categories
- Often the highest-leverage step between “EDA” and “Modeling”

> “Better data beats better algorithms” — Andrew Ng

---

# Feature Workflow

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  A[Raw columns] --> B[Transform / clean]
  B --> C[Engineer new features]
  C --> D[Validate + document]
  D --> E[Model-ready table]
```

- Keep transformations reproducible in R scripts/Rmd
- Version engineered tables or rebuild from scratch each run

---

# Laser League Ingredients

```r
ENIA_ROOT <- "~/ENIA-5120"
players <- readr::read_csv(file.path(ENIA_ROOT, "data", "laser_league_players.csv"))
```

Key columns for features:

- Volumetrics: `season_score`, `assists`, `matches_played`
- Rates: `tag_accuracy_pct`, `shield_uptime_pct`, `energy_delta_pct`
- Physical/mental: `stamina_score`, `reflex_score`, `reaction_time_sec`
- Context: `role`, `home_arena`, `preferred_loadout`, `favorite_drink`

---

# Mutate + Across

```r
players_transformed <- players %>%
  mutate(
    score_per_match = season_score / matches_played,
    assist_rate = assists / matches_played,
    high_accuracy = tag_accuracy_pct >= 80
  ) %>%
  mutate(across(
    c(season_score, assists, stamina_score),
    ~ replace_na(., median(., na.rm = TRUE))
  )) %>%
  mutate(
    stamina_adjusted_score = score_per_match * (stamina_score / 100)
  )
```

- Use `mutate()` for ratios + boolean flags
- `across()` lets you treat multiple numeric columns similarly
- Always guard against divide-by-zero and missing values

---

# Binning & Buckets

```r
players_binned <- players_transformed %>%
  mutate(
    score_bucket = case_when(
      score_per_match >= 80 ~ "Elite",
      score_per_match >= 60 ~ "Competitive",
      TRUE ~ "Needs Coaching"
    ),
    accuracy_bucket = cut(tag_accuracy_pct,
      breaks = c(0, 60, 75, 90, 100),
      labels = c("Low", "Medium", "High", "Pro")
    )
  )
```

- Bucketing helps with interpretability + logistic models
- Store bucket definitions in one place so homework writeups stay consistent

---

# Interactions + Aggregations

```r
players_features <- players_binned %>%
  group_by(squad_id) %>%
  mutate(
    squad_avg_score = mean(season_score, na.rm = TRUE),
    squad_rank = dense_rank(desc(squad_avg_score))
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    score_gap_vs_squad = season_score - squad_avg_score,
    assist_x_accuracy = assist_rate * tag_accuracy_pct,
    energy_balance = energy_delta_pct - shield_uptime_pct
  )
```

- Interaction terms capture combined effects (assists * accuracy)
- Group-level aggregates provide context (player vs squad average)

---

# Feature Checklist

- [ ] Every new column has a clear name + definition
- [ ] No engineered column introduces NAs accidentally
- [ ] Ratios protect against divide-by-zero
- [ ] Buckets include all edge cases (>= vs >)
- [ ] Save engineered tibble (e.g., `players_features`) for future labs/homework
